requirements.title: Only the responsible or an authorised operator changes the dataset
requirements.statement: The application shall refuse every request to introduce, modify or update the information of a battery's passport dataset, from the assembly of the dataset to its delivery to the passport service provider, unless the requester acts for the economic operator responsible for that passport or for an operator to which that economic operator has given a written authorisation recorded in the application.
requirements.rationale: SyR-PASS-005 refines StR-PASS-005 (Art. 77(4) second sentence, Art. 78(f)) as an access decision at the system boundary: one capability decides it and the refusal is the default (invariant 4, deny by default). The written authorisation must be recorded so that the decision can be made and audited. Whether recyclers and repairers that are neither responsible nor authorised may write is Q-971.
requirements.appliesFrom: 18 February 2027 (Art. 77(1))
requirements.notes: SyR-LIFE-144 (end of the passport recorded without the successor's authorisation) is the one exception to SyR-PASS-005 after the waste status, which decision D8 and Annex B point 17 of the CX-0160-4 amendment proposal state.

requirements.title: Every dataset field marked with exactly one access group
requirements.statement: The application shall deliver with each battery's dataset an access marking that assigns every field the dataset holds to exactly one access group of Art. 77(2): the general public (Annex XIII point 1), persons with a legitimate interest and the Commission (point 2), notified bodies, market surveillance authorities and the Commission (point 3), or persons with a legitimate interest (point 4).
requirements.rationale: SyR-PASS-011 refines StR-PASS-013 (Art. 77(2)(a) to (c), Art. 77(6), Art. 78(b)). The passport service provider grants access by these groups (CX-0160-3 5.2), so it needs the group of each field from the economic operator. No field of the CX-0160 models carries a group, so the marking is delivered beside the seven aspects; its form is not decided (finding). The four groups are the headings of Annex XIII points 1 to 4.
requirements.appliesFrom: 18 February 2027 (Art. 77(1))
requirements.notes: When the Commission adopts the implementing act under Art. 77(9), the access group of the Annex XIII point 4 information changes to the purchaser of the battery and the purchaser's agent (SyR-PASS-219, decision Q-1002); SyR-PASS-011 then changes with the wording of the adopted act.

requirements.title: Recovered materials readable by recycler, manufacturer and authorities only
requirements.statement: The application shall grant reading the recovered materials recorded for a battery only to the recycler that recorded them, to the manufacturer of record of the battery's passport and to the authorities, and refuse it to every other subject, including a request without sign-in.
requirements.rationale: SyR-PASS-210 is an owner's rule (the project guidelines of the battery passport application circularity vocabulary, the column access matrix) as an access decision with a refusal by default. Decision Q-702 (who may read the recovered materials of a recycled battery) confirms the tier as a project rule, because the stored Art. 71 sets recycling targets and grants no access right, and names the manufacturer of record of the passport that the recycling ends: the operator that placed that battery on the market, which for a passport created by re-use, repurposing or remanufacturing is the treating operator and not the manufacturer of an original passport. Whether the record belongs to the dataset is Q-971 (whether operators without passport responsibility may record passport information).

requirements.title: Status waste set on the existing passport, with no new passport
requirements.statement: When a battery becomes a waste battery, the application shall set the status 'waste' in that battery's existing passport dataset, keeping its unique identifier and creating no new passport.
requirements.rationale: SyR-LIFE-008 refines StR-LIFE-009 (status waste recorded on the battery passport). The passport stays the existing one because Art. 77(7) first subparagraph, held in StR-LIFE-019 (new passport when a treated battery is placed on the market again), gives a new passport only after preparation for re-use, preparation for repurposing, repurposing or remanufacturing, and the second subparagraph, held in StR-LIFE-050 (responsibility moves when the battery becomes waste), transfers the responsibility for the same passport. Decision Q-022 (whether waste status and recycling are recorded as separate events) records the change when the battery becomes waste, and the recycling as a separate later event that ends the passport; the measure records the change as a change of status of its own.
requirements.appliesFrom: 18 February 2027 (Art. 77(1)), for each LMT battery, each industrial battery with a capacity greater than 2 kWh and each electric vehicle battery placed on the market or put into service

requirements.title: Individual battery information shared with the passport issuer under contract
requirements.statement: When a contract between the owner of a battery and the economic operator that issued the battery's passport exists, the application shall make the information of Annex XIII point 4 of Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 on that battery available to that economic operator through the Catena-X connector.
requirements.rationale: SyR-PASS-215 states use case UC-1, which Francesco named on 2026-11-05. Art. 5(1) of the Data Act (StR-DATA-005) gives the user of a connected product the right to have the data holder make the product data available to a third party, and Art. 78(c) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 (StR-PASS-972) makes the economic operator responsible for the passport store the passport data, so the flow from the owner to the issuer supplies the data that the issuer stores in the passport.
requirements.notes: Gap: draft Art. 2(4) of the Art. 77(9) implementing act (SRC-EU-DRAFT-IMPL-77-9) lists no exception for the economic operator that issued the passport as a recipient of the Annex XIII point 4 information; the bases of SyR-PASS-215 are Art. 78(c) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 and Art. 4(1) and 5(1) of the Data Act (SRC-DATA-ACT). Draft Art. 2(4)(e) lets the economic operator placing the battery on the market authorise the sharing, which can cover the issuer's own receipt once the act is adopted (reading for Francesco). The draft purposes of Art. 2(1) do not name the storage of the passport data by the issuer. The CX-0160 amendment proposal of step 5 states UC-1 with both bases and names the gap.

requirements.statement: When the application records the recycling of a battery for a recycler customer, the application shall send a notification of the end of the battery's passport, naming the passport, the date of the recycling and the recycler, to the data provider of that passport, to the manufacturer that the passport's public nameplate names and to the successor from whom the recycler received the battery.

Decision Q-1006 (option B plus D, approved on 2026-11-09) chose a direct notice from the recycler, because the producer of the ended passport finances the data gathering and reporting (Art. 56(4)(d)). The recycler cannot read the restricted lifecycle record of the passport, so the proposal reaches the producer through the public nameplate and the successor. The notification names the passport, the date and the recycler and carries no recovered materials, because Table 4.4 of the proposal references the material recycling certificate instead.
requirements.notes: No stored text obliges the recycler to report to a manufacturer (StR-LIFE-962, Annex B point 4 of the proposal); the notice rests on the producer's financing of the treatment. SyR-PASS-210 (recovered materials readable by recycler, manufacturer and authorities only) sets who reads the recovered materials. Decision D16 is point for discussion D-4 of Annex D for the Catena-X Digital Product Passport Expert Group. Criterion CX-0160-4-CAC-009 (end of the passport) of the proposal checks the rule.

requirements.title: End of the passport recorded without the successor's authorisation
requirements.statement: After the recycling of a battery whose passport records a successor, the application shall record the end of that passport even when the successor has given no written authorisation for changes of the passport.
requirements.rationale: Section 2.1.5 item 5 of the CX-0160-4 amendment proposal lets the data provider change a passport after the waste status only under the successor's written authorisation (decision D8), except the record of the end of the passport, which the data provider makes in every case (Annex B point 17). requirements.appliesFrom: 18 February 2027 (Art. 77(1))
requirements.notes: SyR-LIFE-144 is the one exception to SyR-PASS-005 (only the responsible or an authorised operator changes the dataset) after the waste status, and SyR-PASS-005 names the exception in its notes. SyR-PASS-005 together with SyR-LIFE-049 (responsibility moves to a named successor when the battery becomes waste) already states decision D8. Criterion CX-0160-4-CAC-007 of the proposal checks the rule.

requirements.title: Manufacturer identification of a passport never changed after issue
requirements.statement: The application shall refuse every change of the manufacturer identification of a battery passport after the passport is issued, so that the original passport keeps the original manufacturer and a new passport keeps the second-life operator that issued it.
requirements.rationale: Art. 78(g) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 requires data authentication, reliability and integrity, and Art. 78(f) restricts the right to modify passport information. DIN DKE SPEC 99100 §6.1.2.4 a), NOTE, separates the manufacturer of the battery from the responsible economic operator, who may change over the battery's life: the operator changes, the manufacturer does not. SyR-LIFE-051 (operator placing the treated battery named as its manufacturer) leaves the original manufacturer on the original passport, and SyR-LIFE-019 links the new passport to the original passport, so the original manufacturer stays traceable. No requirement before 2026-11-11 forbade the change, and the recycle step of the code overwrote the manufacturer.
requirements.notes: The guard sits in the database, so that no code path, script or manual statement under the application roles changes the manufacturer identification; the migrator role sets it once at the migration of the existing demo rows, which receive an arbitrary manufacturer because the data is not live (Francesco, 2026-11-11).
